Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Intake Brief — REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine is a single flat monorepo where every example game is co-located with the shared engine code. This couples game development to the full repository, makes it hard to version or reuse the engine independently, and prevents building lean distributions that bundle only a selected subset of games.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer (primary)** — Maintains shared engine modules and the Gym demo suite; wants a standalone core-engine repo that can evolve, be versioned, and be pulled into any distribution without dragging all games along.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer I can work on `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai` and the Gym in one repo, so that engine changes do not require touching game repos.
- **Game developer** — Builds a single example game in isolation; wants to check out just that game plus the engine and run `npm run dev` / `npm test` / `npm run build` without cloning every other game.
  - *Story:* As a game developer I can clone `tce-golf` (or any game repo) which pulls the core engine as a submodule, so that I can iterate on that game with a fast, focused checkout (`tce-game = distribution with 1 game`).
- **Distribution builder / launcher maintainer** — Assembles and ships a playable bundle (web + desktop binary) that contains the core engine plus a chosen set of 1..n games.
  - *Story:* As a distribution builder I can configure which game submodules are checked out in the launcher repo and run `npm run build` / `npm run package` to produce a web build and an Electron binary that show only the included games in the Game Selector.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core-engine repo defined and extractable** — A standalone core-engine repository exists (or a concrete extraction plan + script is delivered) containing everything shared across games: `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards` (if shared), the Gym (`example-games/gym`), the launcher shell (`src/ui/GameSelectorScene`, `src/ui/createCardGame`), Electron launcher (`electron/`), shared assets under `public/assets`, and shared configs (`tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json` engine dependencies). Git history for moved files is preserved where feasible.
2. **Per-game repos with reverse submodule** — Each example game (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto) has its own GitHub repo with a consistent layout that pulls the core engine as a git submodule for standalone development; `npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, and `npm test -- --project unit` (or equivalent targeted run) succeed in a `game + engine` checkout and path aliases (`@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) resolve correctly across the submodule boundary. Documented exception: games may vendor only their own `example-games/<game>/` tree.
3. **Launcher distribution assembles N games via submodules** — The main Tableau-Card-Engine repo acts as the launcher/distribution repo: it bundles the core engine plus a configurable set of games checked out as git submodules (e.g. under `games/` or `example-games/`), the Game Selector enumerates only the checked-out games, and `npm run build` (web, `dist/` with `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` base) and `npm run build:electron` / `npm run package` (desktop binary via Electron) succeed for any selection of 1..n games including the boundary cases of 1 game and all games.
4. **Dev workflows and Gym preserved** — `npm run dev` (HMR on port 3000), `vite`/`tsconfig` alias resolution, and the Gym demo scenes all continue to work from the core-engine repo and from the launcher distribution; Gym remains the canonical core-engine feature demonstrator and does not move to a game repo.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — `npm run build` succeeds and the relevant test profile passes in the launcher distribution with its default game set (full suite on release; unit + build at minimum before any push per AGENTS.md quality gates).

## Constraints

- Integration mechanism is **git submodules** (option a) — not npm packages or npm workspaces. No npm publication of the engine in this phase.
- **No CI required** in this phase — neither the core-engine repo nor the per-game repos need new GitHub Actions pipelines; existing `pr-checks.yml` / `package.yml` / `deploy.yml` remain on the launcher repo as-is.
- The launcher repo remains the deployable web + Electron distribution; game repos do not deploy independently.
- Preserve permissive-license posture (MIT / CC0) and existing toolchain (Phaser 4 RC, TypeScript strict, Vite, Vitest, Electron).
- Avoid breaking existing developer workflows more than necessary; submodule setup must be documented with copy-paste commands (`git clone --recurse-submodules`, `git submodule update --init --recursive`).
- Keep changes surgical — do not speculatively introduce versioning, changelogs, or release automation beyond what is needed to make the submodule composition build.

## Existing State

- Flat monorepo with a single `package.json` (v0.1.15), single `vite.config.ts` (path aliases for `@core-engine`, `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@ui`, `@ai`), single `tsconfig.json`, and single `index.html` / `main.ts` unified entry point that hard-imports every game scene and registers them in `GAMES` for `GameSelectorScene`.
- Shared engine code under `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`); example games under `example-games/` (gym, golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto); Gym is the interactive demo suite for core-engine features.
- Electron launcher under `electron/` with `build:electron` / `start:electron` / `package` scripts; `.gitmodules` does not exist; production build targets GitHub Pages at `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` and desktop binaries via `electron-builder`.
- Tests under `tests/` with Vitest projects (unit, browser, smoke, dev, tutorial E2E); game scenes and core modules are tightly coupled via static imports in `main.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Extract a **core-engine repository** that owns all shared code plus Gym and the launcher shell (GameSelector, Electron host). The extraction should be reproducible and preserve history (e.g. via `git filter-repo` / `git subtree` or a documented manual move — exact tooling is an implementation detail but must be recorded).
- Move each **example game to its own GitHub repo** (one repo per game, consistent layout). Each game repo composes a runnable project by pulling the core engine as a git submodule — i.e. a game checkout is itself a minimal TCE distribution with 1 game. Submodule pointer + local Vite/TS configs make engine imports resolve without publishing a package.
- Retain the **main Tableau-Card-Engine repo as the launcher/distribution repo** that composes the core engine with any subset of game submodules. Provide a simple mechanism (submodule presence, config file, or CLI flag) to specify which games are included in a given build, so `npm run build` and `npm run package` produce a distribution containing exactly 1..n games (web + binary). The Game Selector must discover games dynamically from the checked-out set rather than hardcoding all imports.
- Update docs (`README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `public/assets/CREDITS.md` where relevant) and add submodule setup / distribution-build instructions. No new CI or npm publishing is required in this phase.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Split / slim per-repo manifests; launcher and game repos need correct deps and scripts (`dev`, `build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `test`).
- `vite.config.ts` — Alias resolution must work across submodule boundaries; launcher needs dynamic game discovery instead of static imports.
- `tsconfig.json` — Path aliases and `include` paths must cover submodule layouts.
- `main.ts` — Unified entry point / GameSelector registration; must become dynamic (enumerate checked-out games rather than hardcoding all scenes).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Game catalogue / registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`); needs to handle a variable game set.
- `src/core-engine/**`, `src/card-system/**`, `src/rule-engine/**`, `src/ui/**`, `src/ai/**`, `src/balance-cards/**` — Shared engine code that stays in core.
- `example-games/gym/**` — Stays in core as the engine feature demonstrator.
- `example-games/<game>/**` — Each moves to its own repo (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto).
- `electron/**` — Launcher host; stays in core/launcher, must build against the composed distribution.
- `public/assets/**` — Shared card/back assets stay in core; game-specific assets move with their game or are documented as shared vs. game-owned.
- `index.html` — Entry HTML; must work in both core-only and composed builds.
- `.gitmodules` (new) — Submodule declarations for launcher→games and game→core compositions.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` — Require updates for new repo layout, submodule workflows, and distribution builds.
- `scripts/**` — Build/test helpers (e.g. `run-ci-tests.sh`, `vite-transcript-plugin.ts`, `build-electron-main.mjs`) may need path adjustments.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)` — completed — established the current flat-monorepo structure, toolchain, and path aliases that this refactor will decompose.
  - `Create a Gym (CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S)` — completed — Gym is the canonical core-engine demonstrator that must remain in the core repo per producer direction.
- **Potentially related docs (paths):**
  - `README.md` — repo layout, quick-start, deployment model.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — project structure, path aliases, adding a game, building/packaging.
  - `AGENTS.md` — monorepo layout, SLL requirement, quality gates, worklog rules; needs updating for the new multi-repo model.
  - `vite.config.ts` / `tsconfig.json` — alias and build configuration that must span submodules.
  - `main.ts` / `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — current static game registration that must become dynamic.
  - `electron/launcher-config.ts` / `electron/content-locator.ts` — desktop content resolution for the launcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Submodule ergonomics** — Git submodules are notoriously easy to misuse (detached HEAD, forgotten `--recurse-submodules`). *Mitigation:* document exact clone/update commands, add a `scripts/setup.sh` or `npm run setup` helper if helpful, and keep the default launcher checkout including a known-good game set.
- **History preservation vs. effort** — Preserving full git history for moved files adds complexity (`filter-repo`/`subtree`). *Assumption:* history preservation is preferred but not blocking — a well-documented move with a single squashed history is acceptable if tooling proves too heavy; record the decision in the implementation plan.
- **Dynamic GameSelector discovery** — Replacing static imports with dynamic discovery (filesystem or manifest) may require Vite glob imports or a small codegen step. *Mitigation:* prototype the discovery mechanism early; keep a fallback static list for the initial cut.
- **Asset ownership ambiguity** — Some assets under `public/assets/` are shared vs. game-specific. *Mitigation:* audit `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game asset usage; move only clearly game-owned assets with their game.
- **Scope creep** — Versioning, npm publishing, per-game CI, and release automation are natural follow-ons but are explicitly **out of scope** for this epic. *Mitigation:* file them as separate follow-up work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** No CI or npm publication is required in this phase (per producer). Web + binary builds from the launcher are sufficient validation.
- **Assumption:** Core engine contains "everything shared across games" — includes `balance-cards` and the launcher shell; Gym stays in core (per producer).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "How should the core engine be consumed by individual game repos? (a) git submodule/subtrees, (b) npm package, or (c) monorepo workspaces?" — Answer (producer, this session): "(a) git submodule/subtrees." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q1. Research: inspected `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitmodules` (absent), `main.ts` static imports, `electron/` layout — confirmed current flat monorepo with no submodules or workspaces.
- Q: "What stays vs. what moves — which components belong in the standalone core-engine repo? Does Gym stay in core?" — Answer (producer, this session): "core engine contains everything that is shared across games, gym remains in the core." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q2. Research: listed `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`), `example-games/` (8 games + gym), `public/assets/` — confirmed Gym is under `example-games/gym` and shared modules are under `src/`.
- Q: "How should builds and deployments change — CI, versioning, npm publication, per-game deploys, launcher assembly?" — Answer (producer, this session): "no CI, or npm publication yet but we do want to be able to build a web and binary distribution that includes a specified set of games, no CI in the games either, Yes main repo is a launcher." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q3. Research: inspected `package.json` scripts (`build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `package:win/linux/mac`), `vite.config.ts` base handling for Pages vs. Electron, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` deployment section — confirmed current GitHub Pages + Electron packaging from the monorepo.

## Foundational Test-References

- `tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts` — Gym smoke coverage (must keep passing from core/launcher).
- `tests/smoke.phaser4.browser.test.ts` — Phaser 4 smoke.
- `tests/vite-config.test.ts` — Vite alias / build config coverage.
- `tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts` — Electron launcher smoke.
- Full suite (`npm test` / `npm run build`) — release gate for the launcher distribution with its default game set.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MTHTJLES009CRHQ** – Linter auto-fix: engine modules (completed)
- **CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM** – Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (completed)
- **CG-0MQN1BLHH0086LU8** – F2: ActiveEffect infrastructure in state & serialization (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: able, around, break, building, bundled (+23 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)

# Intake Brief: Electron Runtime Game Plugin Loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5)

## Problem Statement

The Electron launcher currently requires a rebuild to add new games — all games are statically imported and registered in `main.ts`. The producer wants a runtime plugin system so that a game can be added to an already-built launcher distribution by dropping in game artifacts and updating a manifest, without rebuilding the launcher itself.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** (primary) — Ships the Electron launcher and wants to add or update games post-build by placing game artifact directories and updating a manifest.
  - *Story:* As a distribution operator, I can drop a game's built artifacts into a `games/` directory and add a manifest entry, so that the launcher picks it up at startup without rebuilding.
- **Engine maintainer** — Ensures dynamically-loaded games are compatible with the core engine version in the launcher.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer, I can declare a required `coreEngineVersion` in a game's manifest, so that the launcher rejects incompatible games with a clear error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Runtime game discovery** — The Electron renderer reads a `games/manifest.json` from the content directory at startup, discovers each game's scene class, metadata (title, description, thumbnail), and registers it dynamically so it appears in the Game Selector alongside statically-registered games.
- **Core version compatibility check** — Each game declares a `coreEngineVersion` (semver range) in its manifest; the launcher checks compatibility at load time and skips incompatible games with a clear error message in the Game Selector UI.
- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Graceful degradation** — If the manifest is missing, malformed, or a game fails to load, the launcher continues with the statically-registered games and logs an error. Incompatible games are hidden from the selector but their presence is noted (e.g., "Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z").
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets).

## Constraints

- **Electron-only** — Web runtime plugin is explicitly out of scope.
- **Build-time presets** are handled in CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 (the parent epic); this is purely the runtime plugin phase.
- **Backwards compatible** — The existing static game registration (hardcoded imports in `main.ts`) must continue to work; the plugin system augments rather than replaces it.
- **No npm publication** of games — games are distributed as artifact directories (Vite library-mode ESM builds).
- **Shared dependencies** — Phaser and core-engine must be externalized (not bundled into game artifacts) to avoid duplication.

## Existing State

- `main.ts` (renderer entry): Static imports of every game scene + static `GAMES` array + Phaser scene registration. No dynamic loading.
- `electron/main.ts`: Loads the renderer from a resolved content directory. Has a `ContentDirectoryProvider` chain for content resolution (bundled → Steam DLC override), but no game discovery logic.
- `electron/launcher-config.ts` + `content-locator.ts`: Content directory resolution with provider chain. Extensible but game-discovery-aware.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`: Reads `GameEntry[]` from Phaser registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`), renders the game selector grid.
- Parent epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 at `plan_complete` will introduce `configs/<preset>.json` for build-time game selection (F3 feature).

## Desired Change

- **Manifest schema**: Define a `games/manifest.json` format with entries containing `id`, `sceneKey`, `title`, `description`, `thumbnail` (relative path), `coreEngineVersion` (semver range), and `entry` (path to the game's ESM entry point).
- **Manifest loader**: A new module (e.g., `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts`) that reads the manifest from the content directory, validates entries, and returns a `GameEntry[]` array that merges with statically-registered games.
- **Version compatibility**: Use a semver range matcher (e.g., `semver.satisfies`) to check `coreEngineVersion` against the launcher's core engine version.
- **Dynamic scene loading**: For each compatible game, use `import()` to load the game's ESM entry point, extract the scene class, and register it with `scene.add(sceneKey, SceneClass)` before booting Phaser.
- **Asset paths**: Thumbnails are loaded from a path relative to the game's artifact directory (e.g., `games/my-game/assets/thumbnail.png`), resolved by the plugin loader.
- **Game Selector integration**: The Game Selector receives the merged list (static + dynamic) and renders them identically. Incompatible games are either hidden or shown with a disabled state and tooltip explaining the incompatibility.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts` — **New file.** Reads manifest, validates entries, loads game chunks dynamically, returns merged `GameEntry[]`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Update to accept dynamically-loaded games; add UI for incompatible game indicators.
- `main.ts` — Update `preBoot` callback to call `GamePluginLoader.load()` and merge with static `GAMES`.
- `electron/main.ts` — May need to expose the resolved content directory path to the renderer (e.g., via `preload.cjs` → `window.TCE.contentDir`) so the plugin loader can find the manifest.
- `electron/preload.cjs` — Add preload bridge for `TCE.contentDir` if not already exposed.
- `package.json` — Add `semver` as a dependency (or use a lightweight alternative).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the `games/manifest.json` schema and plugin loading process.
- `AGENTS.md` — Add plugin loading pattern to the Game Architecture Best Practices section.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Dynamic import() in Electron renderer** — Loading ESM modules dynamically in the Electron renderer (Chromium context) may have path resolution quirks. *Mitigation:* Prototype early; use absolute paths resolved from the manifest's content directory.
- **Shared dependency bundling** — If games bundle their own Phaser/core-engine copies, the result is heavy and may cause class-identity issues (two Phaser instances). *Assumption:* Games are built as Vite library modules with `rollupOptions.external: ['phaser', '@core-engine/*']` so they rely on the launcher's bundled copies.
- **Thumbnail loading** — Electron's `file://` protocol may have CORS restrictions for loading images from `games/*/assets/`. *Mitigation:* Use `fs://` protocol or copy thumbnails to a shared asset location during game registration; or use `nativeImage` API in preload.
- **Scope creep** — Features like hot-reload of plugins, game updates, per-game settings panels, or web runtime support are natural follow-ons but are **out of scope**. *Mitigation:* Document them as linked follow-up opportunities.
- **Assumption:** The `games/` directory lives inside the content directory (resolved by `launcher-config.ts`), e.g., `<contentDir>/games/`.
- **Assumption:** `coreEngineVersion` uses semver ranges (e.g., `"~4.0.0"`) and compatibility is checked via major version (breaking changes) and minor/patch (non-breaking).
- **Assumption:** Games are built with Vite library mode, producing ESM chunks (e.g., `dist/index.js`) that export a `GameScene` class and a `GAME_INFO` object.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Where should the manifest live — in the content directory (`games/manifest.json`) or in Electron's userData (`~/Library/Application Support/TCE/plugins/manifest.json`)?" — Answer (producer, CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 planning session): "In the content directory, alongside game artifacts." Source: planning comment on CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Research: content directory is the game content root resolved by `launcher-config.ts`, so placing the manifest there keeps game artifacts and metadata together.
- Q: "Should dynamically-added games declare a required core version?" — Answer (producer, this session): "Yes — core-engine version." Source: existing description note.
- Q: "What happens to incompatible games in the Game Selector?" — Answer (assumption): "Hidden from the selector, with their incompatibility noted in error logs. Future work could add a disabled entry with a tooltip." Source: reasoned assumption from AC4 draft. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*
- Q: "Should the plugin loader run synchronously (blocking Phaser boot) or asynchronously (show a loading state)?" — Answer (assumption): "Asynchronously, with a brief loading overlay if needed. The `GamePluginLoader.load()` returns a Promise that resolves before the `preBoot` callback completes." Source: reasoned assumption for good UX. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM** – Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (completed)
- **CG-0MTRO7ECL006ID7J** – Integration verification — full build & test suite (blocked)
- **CG-0MQVJ4DIC009K8D8** – Scenario Validation Test (completed)

# Add images for all cards

## Problem Statement

The Main Street card redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN) reserves a 64×64 left-art graphic zone on every card face, but all 162 cards currently display only a placeholder (synergy-coloured rectangle with a single-letter initial). Images must be generated from the `art_notes` descriptions in `card-data.csv`, packaged as PNGs, and embedded into the SVG card rendering pipeline so they appear alongside the card text.

## Users

- **Players**: See distinctive, thematic imagery on every card face in their hand, on the street, and in the market — improving recognisability and atmosphere.
- **Developers**: Have a reproducible image-generation pipeline that produces one PNG per card from `art_notes`, with a safe fallback to a generic placeholder when no image exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card across all families (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff) has an associated 64×64 PNG image file in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
2. Images are named `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`) and are referenced by the SVG card generator, which attempts to embed the corresponding PNG and falls back to a generic placeholder when the file is missing.
3. The `graphicZoneSvg()` function in `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` is updated to embed `<image>` elements for the PNG assets (with a fallback `<rect>` + glyph when the image is unavailable or fails to load).
4. All 162 card entries in `card-data.csv` have an `art_notes` value — cards that previously had none receive a generic placeholder description.
5. The full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Image generation quality**: AI-generated images may not match the intended aesthetic. Mitigation: producer reviews images before committing to the repo; a script to regenerate is preferred over manual editing.
- **SVG `<image>` fallback reliability**: SVG `<image>` elements do not gracefully handle missing files — the zone may render blank. Mitigation: the SVG generator emits the `<image>` element, and when the file is absent, falls back to the existing `<rect>` + glyph placeholder.
- **Licensing**: Generated images must be clearly documented as CC0 / self-authored. Mitigation: update `CREDITS.md` with provenance for every new asset directory.
- **Scope creep**: "Every card" could imply artwork for other example games (Golf, Lost Cities, etc.). Mitigation: scope is strictly Main Street 162 cards.

## Constraints

- Images must be permissive / freely available for commercial use (CC0, MIT, or self-authored).
- The naming convention must be deterministic from the card id so the SVG generator can derive asset keys at runtime without additional configuration.
- SVG `<image>` elements must have proper fallback handling so missing assets do not break rendering.
- The 64×64 zone is at `(8, 8)` on the 140×80 card canvas, so images must fit within that rect.

## Existing State

- `public/assets/cards/` — 52 standard playing-card SVGs (CC0, saulspatz/SVGCards) + 1 card back.
- `public/assets/cards/alternative/webisso/` — 52 playing-card SVGs (MIT).
- `public/assets/cards/lost-cities/` — 61 Lost Cities SVGs (MIT).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — 162 rows; 157 have `art_notes`, 5 are empty.
- `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `graphicZoneSvg()` produces a coloured rectangle + initial glyph; comment notes: "Future work can replace the `<g>` body with a real `<image>` or family-specific icon."
- No 64×64 card art images exist anywhere in the project.

## Desired Change

1. Populate `art_notes` for the 5 cards that currently have none (use a generic placeholder description).
2. Generate 64×64 PNG images for all 162 cards from their `art_notes` descriptions, naming them `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`, `comm-library_64_x_64.png`).
3. Place images in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
4. Update `graphicZoneSvg()` to optionally embed an `<image href="...">` element inside the 64×64 zone, with a `<rect>` + glyph fallback.
5. Update the SVG generation pipeline so the asset key is derived from the card id at runtime.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — populate 5 empty `art_notes`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — update `graphicZoneSvg()` to accept an optional image path and emit `<image>` element
- `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/` — new directory for 64×64 PNG images
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — document provenance of card art images

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN** — Redesign all Main Street cards with 64×64 left-art (created the placeholder zone).
- **CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA** — Add synergy icons to Main Street help panel (complementary asset work).
- **CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 — Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (mentions placeholder-to-final art pipeline).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Image format? — **Answer (producer):** PNG files.
- Q: How will images be created and named? — **Answer (producer):** Producer will provide images; naming convention `<card_name>_64_x_64.png`, derived from card id. Placeholder used if image not found.
- Q: Scope — all card families? — **Answer (producer):** Every family (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
- Q: Placement approach — SVG or external Phaser assets? — **Answer (producer):** Embedded in SVG.
- Q: Cards without art_notes (5 cards)? — **Answer (producer):** Create art_notes; use a placeholder description.

- **CG-0MQ7G3DTJ0082CGR** – Sushi Go: Partial HandView migration (layout only) (completed)

# Intake Brief: Check achievements after each action (not only at end of turn)

## Problem Statement

In Main Street, challenge ("achievement") completion is evaluated only during the end-of-turn **EndCheck** phase, so an action that satisfies a challenge produces no immediate feedback — the tracker, activity log, score bonus, and celebration all wait until the player ends the turn. This makes completed actions feel inert and delays reward feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street players** building a run and pursuing challenges.
- **AI / Monte Carlo / headless** consumers of the engine turn flow, which must behave consistently with the interactive path.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I place a card / make a purchase / perform any action that satisfies an active challenge, I want the challenge to register immediately (tracker, log, bonus, celebration) so the action feels rewarding.
- As a player, if I undo an action that completed a challenge, I want to be warned before the undo aborts/commits, so I don't accidentally lose or keep a completion unintentionally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After **any** action that satisfies an active challenge, the challenge is marked complete **immediately** (no end-of-turn wait): `activeChallenges[].completed = true`, the challenge ID is appended to `state.challengesCompleted`, and a `Challenge completed: <title> (+<pts> pts)` entry is added to `state.activityLog`.
2. Per-action evaluation applies to **all action paths**: the interactive command layer (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) and the engine `executeAction` path used by AI, Monte Carlo, and headless runs. The existing end-of-turn EndCheck evaluation is retained as a safety net for completions caused by the closing phases (Income / Incident).
3. In the interactive scene, the challenge **celebration VFX/SFX fires immediately** after the completing action (respecting reduced-motion), and the end-of-turn celebration does **not** re-fire for a challenge already celebrated mid-turn (no double-celebration).
4. Undoing the most recent action when that action completed a challenge shows a **confirmation warning dialog** that offers to proceed or abort. Choosing **Cancel aborts the undo entirely** (no state change); choosing to proceed **reverts the completion**: removes the challenge from `challengesCompleted`, clears its `completed` flag, removes the corresponding "Challenge completed" activity-log entry, and reverts the score bonus.
5. Redo re-applies the action and re-completes the challenge consistently (completion and celebration are restored on redo without duplicating log entries or celebrations).
6. Unit tests cover: per-action completion via the interactive command path; per-action completion via `executeAction`; no double-celebration at end of turn; undo-cancel leaves the completion and bonus intact; undo-confirm revokes completion, bonus, tracker state, and the activity-log entry; and that deterministic simulation (Monte Carlo / AI) outputs remain valid (or the baseline shift is measured and documented).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, help text, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, correct any text stating challenges are evaluated only at EndCheck / end of turn (e.g. `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`).

## Constraints

- **Producer decision (Q1 = A):** completion is revoked on undo, but the player is given a warning that allows the undo to be aborted. Preserve "no revocation" outside of explicit undo.
- **Producer decision (Q2 = A):** per-action evaluation runs on all paths (interactive + `executeAction`/AI/Monte Carlo/headless).
- **Producer decision (Q3 = A):** immediate celebration after the action; end-of-turn celebration deduped.
- `state.activeChallenges` holds evaluator **functions**, so it must not be deep-cloned — the existing `captureSnapshot`/`safeClone` (`structuredClone` then JSON fallback) silently drops functions. The undo snapshot must capture challenge completion state in a cloneable form (e.g. `challengesCompleted: string[]` plus a per-challenge `completed: boolean[]` captured/restored by index) and never the full `activeChallenges` array.
- The undo snapshot currently captures `activityLog` but **not** challenge state; both must be restored atomically on undo to keep tracker, score, and log consistent.
- Reuse existing infrastructure: overlay dialog pattern (`createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, all overlay children parented into `hudContainer`, depth 199/200/201), celebration animator (`MainStreetAnimator.animateCelebration`), and audio (`SoundManager`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, `SFX_KEYS.CELEBRATE = 'sfx-challenge-complete'`, `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`).
- Do not change the score formula (it already counts `challengesCompleted.length`); only the timing of completion changes.
- Deterministic simulation tests (Monte Carlo, AI win-rate) may shift because challenges now complete earlier; re-baseline or document the shift explicitly.

## Existing State

- `evaluateChallenges(activeChallenges, state)` is called only in `MainStreetEngine.ts` inside `processEndOfTurn` (`~L1606`) and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (`~L1946`), during **EndCheck**. This placement was intentional per CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V, which also established the "once complete, no revocation" rule.
- Interactive actions do **not** use `executeAction`; they dispatch through `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` (via `s.undoManager.execute(cmd)`) from `MainStreetTurnController.ts`. Only `community-favour` (interactive) and the AI/Monte-Carlo/headless paths call `executeAction`.
- `MarketActionSnapshot` (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) captures `activityLog`, `actionsRemaining`, `bankedActions`, etc., but not `challengesCompleted` or per-challenge `completed` flags.
- Celebration VFX/SFX is driven by `TurnResult.newlyCompletedChallenges` and triggered in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn` at end-of-turn.
- `performUndo` / `performRedo` already handle undo/redo UX (log entries, `animateUndoRedo`, refresh) and are the natural home for the warning dialog.

## Desired Change

- Evaluate challenges after every successful action.
- Surface newly completed challenges to the immediate caller so the scene can celebrate at once.
- Make challenge completion part of the undoable action state, with a warning-before-undo when a completion would be reverted.
- Ensure end-of-turn evaluation remains as a safety net without duplicating completions or celebrations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add a thin `evaluateChallengesAfterAction(state): string[]` wrapper (or reuse `evaluateChallenges` directly); keep the completion callback (log + `challengesCompleted`).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — call per-action evaluation after each successful action in `executeAction`; expose newly completed IDs to callers (richer return value or a transient state field); keep EndCheck evaluation as the closing-phase safety net; adjust `executeFullTurn` / `executeCompetitiveDay` so per-action and closing-phase completions are not double-reported.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — evaluate challenges inside each command's forward mutation; extend `MarketActionSnapshot` with `challengesCompleted` and per-challenge completion flags (cloneable form only); record which challenges a command completed so undo can warn about them.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — centralise command dispatch so each command's newly completed challenges are detected and celebrated immediately; implement the undo warning dialog + abort in `performUndo`; dedupe the end-of-turn celebration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — expose/wire a shared command-execution helper if the centralisation lives on the scene.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — new `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog(challengeTitle, onUndo, onCancel)` following the `showSellConfirmation` / `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — reuse `animateCelebration`; add the undo-warning interaction if needed.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/*` — locale keys for the new dialog copy (follow existing i18n conventions).
- `tests/main-street/challenge-celebration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — extend; add per-action and undo-revocation tests.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (and any help/tooltip copy) — update the "evaluated at end of turn / end of game" wording.

## Related work

- CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V — **EndCheck Evaluation & Scoring** (source of the current end-of-turn evaluation and the "no revocation" rule this item amends).
- CG-0MQS46G5U001CYUG — **Challenge celebration VFX and sound** (celebration animator/SFX infrastructure reused here).
- CG-0MMJO7COE009UG48 — **Challenge HUD Tracker** (tracker refresh path).
- CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — **Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (blocked; terminology overlap).
- CG-0MU89K6UT007ZNKA / CG-0MU89K6AB001JQOW — **Document / wire deferred end-of-turn mutation** (may interact with undo and turn-flow sequencing).
- CG-0MTKLPTJP003HDA0 — **Fix activity log, challenges, and integration tests** (recent challenge/activity-log work).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Snapshot correctness:** challenge state must be captured/restored in a cloneable form; cloning `activeChallenges` would drop evaluator functions. Mitigation: capture `challengesCompleted` + completion flags by index.
- **Double-celebration / ordering:** immediate celebration vs end-of-turn celebration could overlap with action animations and the turn presentation sequence. Mitigation: dedupe via idempotent `completed` flags and only celebrate each completion once.
- **Simulation/balance drift:** completing challenges earlier can move score thresholds and end-condition timing in Monte Carlo/AI runs. Mitigation: re-run the Monte Carlo harness and AI win-rate tests; re-baseline or document.
- **Undo/redo atomicity:** restoring `challengesCompleted`, flags, and `activityLog` independently could desync. Mitigation: restore them together; add a test asserting tracker/score/log stay consistent after undo and redo.
- **Undo-warning interaction with animations:** `performUndo` early-returns while `uiPhase === 'animating'`; the dialog must integrate with that guard and not strand the scene in a blocked state. Mitigation: only present the dialog when an undo is otherwise legal, and restore `uiPhase` on both confirm and cancel.
- **Scope creep:** e.g. Steam-achievement sync, revoking completions on non-undo paths, or revamping the tracker. Mitigation: record as linked work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** "achievements" in this item means in-game challenges (`activeChallenges` / `challengesCompleted`), not Steam achievements.
- **Assumption:** the warning dialog fires only when the command being undone actually completed a challenge this turn.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When an action completes a challenge and the player then undoes that action, what should happen?" — Answer (producer): **A — Revoke the completion, with a warning that allows the undo to be aborted.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Which action paths should evaluate challenges per action?" — Answer (producer): **A — All paths: interactive command layer and engine `executeAction` (AI, Monte Carlo, headless).** Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the celebration VFX/SFX fire immediately after the completing action?" — Answer (producer): **A — Immediate celebration after the action, with the end-of-turn celebration deduped.** Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143** – Rebalance card families across progression tiers (incl. tiering staff cards) (completed)
- **CG-0MLTSZI651HIVNM3** – Create GitHub Actions deploy workflow (completed)
- **CG-0MSN19DB4008TMPC** – Test contract: turn-limit end conditions (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: action, check, checked, complete, currently, end, every, rather, should, turn

## Root Cause

Not CPU-contention flakiness. The test now fails deterministically (~4 of 5 isolated runs at current `dev`).

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the Coloretto heuristic AI take gate to `netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD` (`TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`). A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers and never sets `flightCard`, so the test's fourth `waitForCondition` (`phase === 'animating' && flightCard !== null`) can never be satisfied; the round ends and phase becomes `round-scoring`.

Full investigation and evidence are recorded in the Plan-investigation comment.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout current `dev`: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts -t "Last Round card"`
3. Repeat several times: the failure depends on whether the AI's first turn drew a bonus card.

## Impact

Blocks the Coloretto browser suite on `dev`. The AI change is intended behaviour; the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part.

## Recommended Fix Direction

Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

## Key Files

- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot` passes reliably against the latest `dev` (e.g. 10 consecutive isolated runs, plus a normal suite run), with the AI's final turn either a place or a take.
2. The test no longer depends on the AI's strategy choice or on a specific shuffled deck (no new flakiness under CPU contention).
3. Documentation is updated only if the fix changes documented behaviour; a test-only fix requires no doc change.
4. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun the test locally several times.
2. Root cause is known (see above); route to implementation.

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Root-cause investigation: Plan-investigation comment on this work item
- Related: CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4 (AI `wholeRowValue` take-gate change)
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# Feature: Per-game repos use `src/` source root with alias-based core imports (Option C)

Part of epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Follow-on refinement of the F4 game-repo scaffold.

## Goal

As a game developer I can clone a `tce-<game>` repo and find that game's source at the repo-root `src/` directory, with every engine import going through the `@core-engine/*` (and `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) path aliases, so that the repo has an idiomatic layout and does not rely on the `src -> ../tableau-card-engine-core/src` compatibility symlink or fragile `../../src/**` relative imports.

## Problem

The F4 scaffold keeps the game nested at `example-games/<game>/` and creates a `src` symlink into the core checkout. 319 game-source imports use `../../src/**` and only resolve because the game sits exactly two levels below the repo root. This is fragile, non-idiomatic, and blocks moving the game source to `src/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Decision record exists (child C1) fixing the per-game layout (`src/**` or `src/<game>/**`), how `scripts/`, `example-games/gym`, shared assets and test helpers resolve from `src/`, and the `scenePath` contract for monorepo-local vs sibling-repo contexts.
2. A scaffolded `tce-<game>` checkout has its game source under `src/`, contains no `src` symlink to the core, and `npm run build` + `npm test -- --project unit` succeed.
3. No game-repo source or test imports core through a `../../src/**` relative specifier; a test/lint guards this invariant.
4. The launcher (`configs/*.json` presets + `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) resolves game scenes in both the flat monorepo (`example-games/<game>/…`) and the `src/` sibling game-repo layout; the 1-game (`solo`) and all-games (`full`) presets both build.
5. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md` describe the new per-game layout.

## Constraints

- The monorepo/launcher flat layout may stay `example-games/<game>/`; only per-game repos change to `src/`. C1 may override this if a uniform layout proves cleaner.
- The producer gate on F4 still applies: no GitHub repo creation or push.
- Engine imports must resolve via `tsconfig.json` `paths` + Vite `resolve.alias`; no new npm publication of the engine.

## Children

- C1 Decide per-game `src/` layout, import contract and preset resolution
- C2 Codemod game source + tests off `../../src/**` to engine aliases
- C3 Extraction/scaffold/repo-layout emit the `src/` layout
- C4 Discovery plugin + launcher presets resolve `src/` sibling layouts
- C5 Update game docs and verify per-game tsc/build/unit

# Task C4: Discovery plugin + launcher presets resolve `src/` sibling layouts

Parent: F9 CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME (part of epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17).
Depends on: C1 (scenePath contract).

## Goal

As a distribution builder the launcher resolves a game's scene whether the game is in the flat monorepo (`example-games/<game>/…`) or in a `src/`-layout sibling repo (`../tce-<game>/src/…`), so `npm run build` works for the `solo` (1 game) and `full` (all games) presets after the layout change.

## Scope

1. Implement the C1 `scenePath` contract in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (`discoverGames`, local vs sibling resolution) and `configs/*.json` presets (`full`, `solo`, `arcade`, `deluxe`, `core-only`).
2. Keep `core-only` (Gym, no games) working.
3. Game repos keep their own `configs/game.json` valid for the `src/` local layout (coordinate with C3).
4. Update the plugin unit tests (`tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`) with a `src/`-layout sibling fixture and an error case for a missing scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Plugin resolves both flat-monorepo and `src/` sibling layouts; unit tests green.
2. `GAMES_CONFIG=configs/solo.json npm run build` and `GAMES_CONFIG=configs/full.json npm run build` succeed in the launcher against composed siblings; the selector enumerates exactly the configured games.
3. `GAMES_CONFIG=configs/core-only.json npm run build` still succeeds (Gym only).
4. Fail-fast, actionable error when a configured sibling scene is absent.

## Key Files

- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`
- `configs/*.json`
- `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`

C5 implemented (docs + per-game gate verification).

Docs:
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 (updated in C3) describes the emitted `src/` layout, the removed symlinks and their alias replacements.
- `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md` gains a "How to work with a `src/`-layout game repo" section with copy-paste extract/scaffold/dev/build/test commands and the explicit import rules.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`: the scaffold section and the multi-repo/adding-a-game sections now describe the `src/` layout, the full alias set and the absence of the `src`/`scripts`/`gym`/`tests-helpers` symlinks.
- `README.md`: the discovery-resolution note now describes the three-step local -> sibling `src/` -> legacy-sibling order, and the per-game loop notes the `src/` layout and alias contract.
- AC4 checked: no developer doc instructs using the removed `src` symlink or `(../)+src/**` imports.

Scaffold portability fixes found by the gate:
- Inherited `package.json` scripts that referenced `example-games/<game>/...` are repointed to `src/...`.
- `rewriteGameTreePaths` now also walks `.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.js` (game `.mjs` generators hardcode `example-games/<game>/...` paths) and repoints quoted core-owned CLI paths (`'scripts/replay.ts'` -> `'core/scripts/replay.ts'`) and core-layer scan roots (`'src/ui'` -> `'core/src/ui'`).

Evidence (scaffolded single-game checkout, core = this worktree; each test repo `git init`-ed so `git rev-parse HEAD` works):

| Game | `tsc --noEmit` | `npm run build` | `npm test -- --project unit` |
|------|----------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| golf | exit 0 | ✓ built (dist/) | 11 files / 217 passed, 5 skipped |
| main-street | exit 0 | ✓ built (dist/) | 233 files / 3883 passed, 3 skipped |

Launcher checks: `npm run build` green; terminology guard PASS; `npm test -- --project unit` green (414 files / 7140 tests).

Note: the main-street fixture needed the game-owned assets (`public/assets/games/main-street/`), `docs/main-street/` and `tests/fixtures/` + `tests/helpers/` to mirror a real extraction; all are produced by `extract-repos.sh`.
